The group 1344 = 8 × 168 acting on the seven kites

Signed permutations of the octonion units that keep the table; their action on the seven struts; the eight sign changes that fix every kite. A picture shows a structure; it is not evidence that the structure means anything beyond its definition.

← Box-kite gallery

About this visual

What you are looking at. The group of the labelled octonions: signed permutations of e1…e7 that keep the octonion multiplication table. Found here by trying all 5040 permutations (168 keep the Fano lines) and all 128 sign patterns on each (8 survive per permutation): 1344 elements in all. Each acts on the seven box-kites by permuting their struts.

How to read it. Left: the seven struts on a ring, the arrows s → π(s) of one chosen permutation, its cycles colour-coded. Choose a cycle type or step through the 168. Right: the census of cycle types, the eight sign changes that fix every kite, and the numbers that make 1344 = 8 × 168.

What it shows. The 168 permutations have cycle types 1 + 21 + 42 + 56 + 48 = 168: the identity, 21 involutions with three fixed points, 42 of type 4·2·1, 56 of type 3·3·1 and 48 seven-cycles. The 1344 act TRANSITIVELY on the 168 unit zero-divisor points with a point stabiliser of order 8, and extend to the sedenions. The extension 2³·PSL(2,7) does not split: no subgroup of order 168 maps onto the 168 permutations (all 64 lifts of a generating pair span the whole group of order 1344).

What it does not show. That 168 = |PSL(2,7)| acts regularly on the 168 points: it does not, because the points are an orbit of the group of order 1344 and the stabiliser has order 8. And it is not the full automorphism group of the sedenions, which is not computed here.

Numbers to check. 168 Fano permutations; 1344 signed; kernel 8 = 2³; 168 points, one orbit, stabiliser 8; cycle types {1111111: 1, 22111: 21, 421: 42, 331: 56, 7: 48}; 64 lift pairs, all spanning 1344, so split = false.

running self-check…

Code and data. Everything shown is recomputed in the browser by bk.js (the Cayley–Dickson table by doubling, every product, the group by enumeration) and compared with the numbers the Python engine baked into bk_data.js.

  • ValaQuenta/modules/box_kite/maths.py: the Python engine these pages port and check against (Cayley–Dickson table, assessors, box-kites, associator, the labelled group)
  • ValaQuenta/wiki/box_kite.md: the engine's record page, including 'The group, enumerated'
  • Ainulindale/wiki/84_the_box_kite_debugger.md: the narrative of the box-kite as a debugger
  • ValaQuenta/tests/test_box_kite.py: the tests, including an independent recursive Cayley–Dickson product
